It passed in a few days, though. Not sure what caused it.  

The worst part is I’ve thought about how things could end. I’ve imagined driving out to the lake late at night, leaving the car running in the garage. It scares me, but it also feels like the only way out sometimes. I haven’t told anyone, not even my doctor.

Lately, I’ve just felt… stuck. For about the last ten months, it’s been hard to get out of bed some days—my body feels so heavy, like I’m moving through water. I love my kids at school, but even teaching feels harder now. I don’t have the energy I used to, and I keep second-guessing everything. What outfit should I wear? What to eat? Even small choices feel overwhelming, and I’ll stand in front of the fridge for minutes just paralyzed. I’ve started canceling plans with friends—calls go unanswered, texts linger. It’s not that I don’t care, I just… can’t reach out.  

But sometimes—maybe a few times over the past year—things felt different. I’d suddenly sleep less, not because I was anxious, but because my mind was racing, and I felt almost electric. I’d clean the apartment at midnight or plan these big projects. It didn’t feel bad—actually, it felt great at the time. But it never lasted more than a few days, and it didn’t mess up work or get me in trouble. So I don’t know if that means anything. Most of the time, I’m just… drained. I worry I’m losing myself, but I’m not sure what’s going on.

I’m a special ed teacher, and I used to love planning activities and connecting with the kids, but now I feel exhausted all the time. Just getting out of bed is hard. My body feels like it’s full of sand—getting dressed, commuting, even brushing my teeth takes so much effort.

I’ve been skipping dinners with friends, not returning calls. I don’t even feel like texting anyone. At first, I thought I was just stressed, but now I can’t even decide what to eat or what to wear in the morning. I stand in front of my closet for ten minutes, paralyzed. I’ve had moments where I felt restless, wired—like three months ago when I barely slept for a few days and was rearranging my entire apartment at midnight—but it didn’t last, and I crashed back into this deep fatigue. That’s never happened before. My doctor asked if I’ve ever had those highs before—manic episodes or anything—and I haven’t. This is the first time I’ve felt anything like this.

I even maxed out my credit card on supplies I didn’t need. I felt like I could solve everyone’s problems.  

I know that sounds kind of wild now, but at the time, it didn’t feel wrong—just unstoppable. Looking back, that high lasted over a week and ended when I completely crashed into this current fog. That’s when the exhaustion and sadness took over and never really left.

I wake up each morning with this deep hollow in my chest—like I’m just going through motions, but the reasons for them are gone. Even small things—what to eat, what to wear—feel impossible. I stand there in front of the same few clothes, clock ticking in my head, paralyzed.

I’m tired all the time. Not from work—there’s not much to do, and I can't even bring myself to finish the basic logs some days. My body feels heavy, like the air’s thicker out here.

But… there were a few nights—maybe three or four weeks back—when I didn’t sleep for two, three days straight. I cleaned the whole tower, rewired the old radio for no reason, felt wired, like my thoughts were racing. Felt almost good—until it wasn’t. I don’t know what that was. Maybe just cabin fever. Maybe too much coffee. It passed quick. I just don’t want to lose this job. I need the quiet. But sometimes… the quiet feels too loud.
